absences.note: S1 has no approval states, no session worklist; only paper triage queue (K40/K41, object paper). S2-S4: server-side status mirror and admin worklist reports of sessions needing approval (K39), paper curation priority (K42); no enforced ordering, priority queue or next-session rule for pending sessions at any snapshot.

S1: curs.assigned_curator settable by admins (K26). S2-S4: curs_curator assignment, admin create/reassign/send (K27, K30, K43), curator self-reassignment (K28), exported sessions not reassignable (K29). No reviewer assignment field (the approver is whoever starts approval, K11), no due dates, no reminders that change state at any snapshot. Reminder-like e-mails that do not change state: admin-triggered send/re-send of session link (Tools::send_session, session_resent template, S2+), session_accepted/reassigned e-mails (S2+), daily summary e-mail to admins (script/canto_daily.pl, added 2013-06-12, S2+).

No expiry, timeout, withdrawal or scheduled job that writes session state at any snapshot (searched remind/expir/stale/abandon/cron/deadline; scripts canto_daily.pl, update_statuses.pl and update_all_statuses.pl only report or recompute cached statuses). S1: only generic Delete::object (any logged-in user) and no export state, recorded as no control. S2-S4: admin-only session deletion (K25), CLI canto_delete.pl --curs (operator, from 2012-02-26), automatic EXPORTED marking on export (K21), S4 manual set_exported_state (K24).

notes: Snapshot S1 (v243, 2012-01-09, PomCur) predates the approval workflow: states were NEEDS_SUBMITTER/NEEDS_GENES/READY and the approval states, admin approval and locking all arrived 2012-01-19..2012-02-18. Uncertainties: (1) K4: at S3/S4 the page-level lock (K3) remains but annotation-changing web services are not refused in NEEDS_APPROVAL/APPROVED (since 2019-06-05) or EXPORTED (since 2020-01-11), so the lock on annotations is in effect client-side at S4; the read-only UI was not coded as a separate C control. At S3 EXPORTED sessions were still fully locked against ws writes. (2) K7 tau: admin-only completion was enforced indirectly from 2012-01-22 via K5 before the explicit croak on 2012-07-25. (3) K16 and K24 have no role check in the server code (any holder of the session link whose request passes the state dispatch), K14 relies on K5 for admin restriction. (4) K22 tau uses the first dump-approved filter (CLI) 2012-03-09; the S4 per-annotation filter dates from 1eb613ba9 2019-03-06. (5) admin_session metadata (set when an admin creates a session, 2012-01-26 'Skip approval step for curators') is stashed and passed to JS but no server-side code skips approval with it at S2-S4, so it is not recorded. (6) Global ACL (K43) and Edit _check_auth are partly generic infrastructure; recorded because they are what restricts session creation/assignment and worklists to admins. (7) Approval timestamps (first_submitted, first_approved, previous_approved, unexported, 2017-2020) are automatic audit records, not coded separately. (8) Message-to-curators notice for admins (2024-03-01) and unused-genotype warning on approval page are display-only, not coded.
